clue.text: Branch of religion found in southern Haifa, oddly

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the odd-numbered places of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A religious tradition said to be present in the south of the Israeli city of Haifa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes letters 1, 3 and 5 of Haifa, giving HIA after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Shia Islam is one of the two main branches of the Muslim faith.

clue.text: Provide info for student inhibited by signal at home

indicators.note: held back or hemmed in by, so the student's letter sits inside the word for signal

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act or speak
L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone briefs a student who has been stifled by a sign while staying home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inhibited by' places the student inside the signal; 'at home' is the familiar sense of being in.
explanation.definitionFit: To clue someone in is an idiom for filling them in with information.

clue.text: Clubs banished from prisons for quite some time

indicators.note: sent away from, so the clubs letter is taken out of the word for prisons

parts.note: cages are places of confinement, here standing for prisons
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Golf or social clubs have been excluded from jails for a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banished from' removes C from CAGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is informal for a very long stretch of time, so 'for ages' means for a long while.

clue.text: Hot food is not healthy, covered in sliced potato mostly

indicators.note: wrapped round by, so the word for unwell sits inside the shortened potato word
most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a chip is a slice of fried potato
ill means not healthy

explanation.surface: A warning that spicy food smothered in fried potato slices is bad for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the potato word to CHI, and 'covered in' wraps that around the word for unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli is the hot pepper, and also a spicy dish such as chilli con carne.

clue.text: So that's your game … wearing old, jaunty headgear!

indicators.note: having on, so the exclamation is clothed by the word for jaunty

parts.note: pert means lively and jaunty
aha is the exclamation of someone who has just seen through a scheme

explanation.surface: Someone exposes a trick while sporting a battered, rakish hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So that's your game' is a whole exclamation standing for three letters; 'wearing' clothes it in the jaunty word.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera hat is a collapsible top hat once worn to evening performances.

clue.text: Poison diffused at this point somewhere up high

indicators.note: spread out and scattered, so the letters of poison are rearranged

parts.note: here means at this point or place

explanation.surface: Toxic gas spreads out at this spot, somewhere high above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diffused' rearranges the six letters into IONOSP; 'Poison' looks like the subject but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The ionosphere is an upper layer of the atmosphere, far above the ground.

clue.text: Complete first section of windmill, house and hotel inside Lego set

indicators.note: the opening part of the word, here just its initial letter
placed within, so the hotel letter goes in the middle of the rearranged toy name
set as in set out or arranged afresh, so the letters of Lego are reordered

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Building instructions: a windmill section, a house and a hotel inside a Lego kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges the toy name into LEOG, and 'inside' slips the hotel letter in to make LEHOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Going the whole hog is an idiom for doing something completely and without reservation.

clue.text: Coming from the south, I'm not impressed about French leaders being gallant

indicators.note: going round, so the turned slang word encloses the French kings
in a down entry, reading from the bottom up means the word runs backwards

parts.note: meh is the slang grunt of someone unimpressed
rois are French kings

explanation.surface: A grumpy observer, unmoved by daring French generals arriving from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming from the south' turns the unimpressed grunt into HEM, and 'about' wraps it round the French kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroism is courage and bravery, the quality of acting gallantly.

clue.text: Fashionable dance music

parts.note: hip means fashionable or trendy
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A description of trendy club music for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip hop is a style of popular music built on rap and beats.

clue.text: Fellow eats a new type of Asian food

indicators.note: takes in, so the word for fellow swallows the other letters

parts.note: a peer is a fellow or equal

explanation.surface: A man tries a new kind of dish from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' puts A and N inside PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Paneer is a fresh cheese used in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Where you can see lots more and also move around

indicators.note: shift about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spot where you can view a great deal more and wander freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' looks like 'a great deal' but means auction lots; 'move around' rearranges the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A saleroom is an auction house where items are put up in numbered lots.

clue.text: Cheese pieces next to eggs on the counter

indicators.note: counter as in running counter or contrary, so the word for eggs is read backwards

parts.note: nits are the eggs of lice
king and bishop are both chess pieces

explanation.surface: A shop scene: slices of something laid beside eggs on the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the counter' turns NITS into STIN; KING and BISHOP are two chess pieces. Stinking Bishop is a pungent English washed-rind cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinking Bishop is a strong-smelling soft cheese from Gloucestershire.

clue.text: Back of crypt in Notre Dame renovated to make space for art

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
done up and rebuilt, so the letters of Notre Dame are rearranged

explanation.surface: Restoring Notre Dame cathedral, with work at the back of its crypt to free up an art space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' rearranges NOTRE DAME into ATEMODERN after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tate Modern is London's national gallery of modern art, in a former power station.

clue.text: Reached cave without using river

indicators.note: leaving out, so the river letter is removed from the cave word

parts.note: a grotto is a small cave

explanation.surface: Someone arrived at a cave without taking the river route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without using' drops R from GROTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Got to is an everyday phrasal verb for arrived at a place.

clue.text: Try crazy flips

indicators.note: turns over, so the word for crazy is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: An attempt at doing mad somersaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flips' turns BATS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab is an attempt, as in having a stab at something.

clue.text: Plot to incorporate one group split in two

indicators.note: to take into itself, so the plot word encloses the others

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
I is the Roman numeral one
a sect is a group of followers

explanation.surface: A scheme to absorb one faction that has broken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a scheme but is a flower bed; 'to incorporate' puts one and the group inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two parts, usually equal halves.

clue.text: Parent of son expelled by teacher

indicators.note: thrown out by, so the son letter leaves the teacher word

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher

explanation.surface: A mother or father whose boy has been thrown out of school by a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelled by' removes S from MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is Latin for mother, old British public-school slang for one's mum.

clue.text: Customer picked up medicine and got back on with things

indicators.note: lifted up, so in a down entry the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a user is a customer of a service

explanation.surface: A shopper collected a prescription and carried on with the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns the customer word into RESU, read upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to restart after a break, carrying on where one left off.

clue.text: Prefer to put back sandwiches containing pork, perhaps

indicators.note: set backwards, so the concealed letters are read in reverse
holds between its ends, so the letters sit inside the words given

explanation.surface: Choosing to put pork back between bread slices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' hides FERT in 'Prefer to', and 'put back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tref is the Yiddish term for food not kosher under Jewish dietary law, such as pork.

clue.text: Nice tutors freely smile and seemed so willing at heart

indicators.note: loosely and without constraint, so all these letters are rearranged
the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Teachers who grin and look so eager deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not 'pleasant'. 'at heart' gives L from willing, and 'freely' rearranges it with SMILE, SEEMED and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: In France, mesdemoiselles are young ladies, and a mademoiselle is also a French governess.

clue.text: Property in Spain, say

parts.note: E is Spain's international vehicle code
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A house or land holding in Spain, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but means STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large landed property, or all of one's possessions.

clue.text: Gift of support that's taken on a charity's case

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A donation of backing that a charity has taken up as its cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes the outer letters of charity, C and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is money or property left to someone in a will, a bequest.

clue.text: Literate: upper-class chap entertained by two senior journalists

indicators.note: hosted by, so the class letter and the chap sit between the two editors

parts.note: ED is editor, a senior journalist, so two of them give ED twice
U is upper-class, as in the British 'U and non-U' usage
cat is jazz-age slang for a chap

explanation.surface: A well-read posh man is wined and dined by two newspaper editors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' puts U and CAT between the two EDs.
explanation.definitionFit: A literate person can read and write well, which comes from being schooled.

clue.text: Deposit of soft sludge rising from the ground

indicators.note: coming up from below, so in a down entry the word is read upwards

parts.note: mud is soft sludge
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A heap of soft muck welling up out of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising from the ground' turns the sludge into DUM; soft is P from music, placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump is to set down or deposit something carelessly.

clue.text: Bot maybe makes all gadgets genuinely operate together from the outset

indicators.note: the outset of each word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A robot that gets all gadgets working together properly from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bot' looks like a robot but is a botfly larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A bot is the larva of the botfly, so it is a kind of maggot.

clue.text: Fine wine, unopened

indicators.note: with its opening gone, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian wine

explanation.surface: A good-quality wine still with its cork in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' drops T from TOKAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay means acceptable or all right, the everyday sense of fine.

clue.text: Most dry grain's bagged by weight

indicators.note: put into a bag, so the grain goes inside the weight letters

parts.note: rye's, the possessive of the cereal rye

explanation.surface: The driest cereal, sacked up and sold by weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bagged by' puts the grain inside the weight abbreviation. 'dry' here is dry humour, not lacking moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: Wry humour is dry and drily mocking, so the wryest is the most drily ironic.

clue.text: Doctor given time at the end with a number of Italian royals

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: N is the mathematical symbol for a number

explanation.surface: A doctor given extra time eventually, along with several Italian princes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number of' looks like 'several' but splits: A, N, then 'of' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicean is the adjective for the Medici, the ruling dynasty of Renaissance Florence.
